hints: The smallest subset includes every negative number and excludes every positive number.
Flipping the inclusion of any element adds its absolute value to that minimum.
Generate the k smallest sums of nonnegative values using a min-heap.
analogy: Start at the cheapest configuration, then pay nonnegative adjustment costs in increasing order.
example: For [-3,1], the minimum is -3. Adjustments 0,1,3,4 produce subset sums -3,-2,0,1.
algorithm: Set base to the sum of negative elements, replace each element by its absolute value, and sort these values. Output base first. If more sums are needed, put (a[0],0) in a min-heap. Repeatedly pop (s,i), output base+s, and if i+1<n push (s+a[i+1],i+1) and (s-a[i]+a[i+1],i+1). Stop after k outputs. Keep equal sums as separate heap entries because different subsets count separately.
correctness: Each subset of sorted nonnegative adjustments has a unique parent: if it contains both its largest and second-largest index, remove the largest; otherwise replace the largest with the preceding index. The two heap transitions reverse these parent operations. Their costs never decrease, so best-first extraction enumerates all subset sums in nondecreasing order, including duplicates.
complexity: For n values and k outputs, sorting takes O(n log n), heap work O(k log k), and space O(n+k).
